_about: Hand-maintained English text for the paper site. bench/build_site.py merges it with the run records under experiments/ and writes site/data.js. Numbers are never typed here: they come from scores.json. sources[*].sequence (the exact clip id) is a record for the group and is never written to the page, so the page does not point at the ground truth of a clip.

repo._note: Where the Code, GitHub and run-record links point. A --public build carries these links only when public is true. The URL names an account, so leave it false while the repository is private or the authors are anonymous.

figure._note: The overview figure in The task (Figure 2), drawn by bench/fig_task_flow.py from one run. The internal build uses run. A --public build uses the first of run, public_runs whose footage source has redistribution ok, because the figure shows frames of the input video.

001.title: Smoke test: a synthetic humanoid clip
001.question: Does the whole pipeline run? The agent watches a rendered video of a humanoid and outputs the trajectory of 29 joints.
001.finding: It runs. The motion is broadly right but the wave is lost: position error is below the frozen pose, velocity error is level with it.

conditions.name: Original video
given: Synthetic video (same renderer as the ground truth)
Humanoid model: kinematics and meshes, make named

002.title: Oracle keypoints instead of video
002.question: Is the error in seeing or in solving? Hand the agent ground-truth keypoints and no video.
002.finding: With ground-truth keypoints the motion is recovered almost exactly. The bottleneck is perception, not fitting.
002.status_note: Diagnostic only: the input is ground-truth keypoints, not video, which is outside the task.

003.title: Render gap
003.question: How much is left when the agent can no longer match its own render to the video pixel for pixel?
003.finding: Changing only the look of the scene already breaks most of the render-and-compare loop; an unknown moving camera breaks more. Telling the agent how the camera moves did not help. Two runs of the same condition differ widely.

004.title: Motion-capture clips retargeted to the humanoid
004.question: Can the agent still recreate fast motion-capture clips with turns and travel?
004.finding: Two clips, one configuration, opposite outcomes. The run records were not kept, so these runs cannot be re-scored with the current metric.
004.status_note: No run records in the repository.

conditions.name: Retargeted mocap clips
given: Humanoid model: kinematics and meshes, make named

005.title: Ready-made tools for the agent
005.question: If rendering, forward kinematics and comparison are handed over as tools, do scores change?
005.finding: The tools were used; of two clips one score rose and one fell, so no effect can be attributed to them. The run records were not kept.
005.status_note: No run records in the repository; the current protocol never hands over a matched renderer.

conditions.name: With a matched rendering toolkit
given: A toolkit that renders the same scene from the same camera
Humanoid model: kinematics and meshes, make named

006.title: No robot appearance
006.question: With a kinematic model only, the agent cannot render what the robot looks like. How much is left?
006.finding: Worse than a frozen pose in both runs. The agents built capsule bodies or hand-labelled keypoints, and lost the depth direction.
006.status_note: Diagnostic only: the current protocol always gives the mesh model.

007.title: Real video: a humanoid, a robot arm, a person
007.question: How far does the agent get when the video is real footage?
007.finding: The calibrated, slow robot arm is recovered well. The real humanoid clips are not: only the fixed-camera side kick beats its frozen pose. The human clip was a keypoint task and has no mesh score.

conditions.name: Robot arm, model withheld
given: Real robot video from a different lab
Joint names, ranges and zero convention

conditions.name: Person, keypoints only
given: Camera intrinsics, extrinsics and world frame

008.title: Three bodies from real video, mesh model given, no calibration
008.question: Given an anonymous mesh model and no camera calibration, can agents recreate the motion of different bodies from real video?
008.finding: Heading, turns and large poses come out right; limbs and timing do not. On all three bodies velocity error stays close to the frozen pose: sparse keyframes with interpolation erase fast motion.
